draft.title: Conclusions
card: A conclusion is the last paragraph of an analytical essay. It closes the argument by returning to the thesis.
It restates the thesis in fresh words. It does not copy the opening sentence.
It draws the argument together by showing how the main steps of the essay built towards the thesis. It may also say why the argument matters, such as what it shows about the text's ideas.
It adds no new evidence. A new quotation or a new point belongs in a body paragraph, not in the conclusion.
draft.remember: A conclusion returns to the thesis in new words and pulls the argument together, with nothing new added.

a.q: Which sentence would best belong in the conclusion of an essay?
opts: Together, these points show the writer treats memory as unreliable
A further quotation from the last chapter also shows this idea
This essay will now argue that memory is unreliable in the text
A symbol is also used, so it is worth noting here as well
a.why: The first option draws the steps together and restates the thesis in fresh words. The second tempts students because it sounds like support, but a conclusion adds no new evidence. The third sounds like an introduction and the fourth adds a new point.
a.clue: A conclusion looks back over the argument, not forward to new material.

b.q: Layla's thesis says a novel shows that power isolates people. Her conclusion repeats that sentence word for word, then adds a new quotation. What is the main problem with it?
opts: It copies the thesis and adds new evidence
It restates the thesis, which a conclusion should avoid
It draws the argument together too much
It explains why the argument matters, which is not allowed
b.why: A conclusion should restate the thesis in fresh words, so copying it word for word is a weakness. A new quotation is also new evidence, which belongs in a body paragraph. Restating the thesis is fine when the wording is changed, so the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Check both things Layla did against what a conclusion should leave out.
